admin.policy.help.actionType: Choose what staff should do: a Site action is something they carry out, a Phone call opens a phone number, and a 311 ticket prepares a report to the City. This choice controls the action available in the app.
admin.policy.help.agency: Name the organization responsible for carrying out or responding to this action. Staff see this name when following progress, so use a recognizable name rather than a technical code.
admin.policy.help.agencyCode: This is a technical agency identifier used when sending a 311 report. It is different from the agency’s display name. Prefer an existing agency setting and ask the integration owner before changing the code.
admin.policy.help.agencyPreset: Choose an existing agency and contact to copy its name, phone number when available, and City agency code. Review the copied details below; choosing a preset does not change the written instruction.
admin.policy.help.aliases: These are older names for this same category, one per line. Saving a renamed category adds its previous name automatically. Keep these names so historical observations still connect to the correct rules.
admin.policy.help.allHours: Enable this when the advice is the same every day at every time. Disable it to set particular hours or days, such as an agency’s opening hours. Other rules must cover the remaining times.
admin.policy.help.answer: Choose the answer that should lead to this action. Yes and No mean the ordinary answer to the question as written. If you reverse a question’s meaning, review both answer branches so the actions are not accidentally reversed.
admin.policy.help.button: Write the words on the action button, such as Call SFFD or File 311 ticket. Use a clear action verb. Changing these words does not change what the button does. Keep multiple existing labels on separate lines.
admin.policy.help.categoriesFile: Choose the categories CSV containing descriptions and severity guidance. Also choose the matching rules CSV. These replace the local draft preview, so export any work you want to keep first.
admin.policy.help.checkTranslations: Include all supported staff languages when checking the draft. Missing translations block release preparation so new instructions are not introduced without the required language versions.
admin.policy.help.day: Choose whether this rule applies on this day of the week. For periods crossing midnight, each observation uses its own local day. Other rules must cover the unselected days.
admin.policy.help.deadline: Set the longest acceptable response time in hours. Enter 0 for an immediate response; an empty field does not mean immediate. This sets the expected response deadline, not an agency’s opening hours.
admin.policy.help.definition: Explain what this category means in a few clear sentences. The app uses this definition when reviewing an observation, so be specific about what belongs here.
admin.policy.help.descriptionGuidance: Explain how the app should describe an observation to staff. For example, ask for factual, neutral wording and tell it not to guess who caused an issue.
admin.policy.help.end: The last minute when this rule applies, in San Francisco time. The whole end minute is included: an end of 17:00 covers through 17:00:59. A following rule would normally start at 17:01.
admin.policy.help.excludes: List similar-looking situations that should not count as this category. This helps keep overlapping categories separate and prevents the wrong advice.
admin.policy.help.guidance: Explain the recommended action in plain language, including any precautions or useful context. This supports the main instruction; it should not contradict it or introduce a different action.
admin.policy.help.inProgress: Enable this if staff may mark the action as still underway while waiting for work or an agency response. Disable it for an action that should not remain in that state.
admin.policy.help.includes: List examples that should count as this category, preferably one per line. Concrete examples help the app recognize the intended problem consistently.
admin.policy.help.jsonFile: Choose a previously exported policy JSON file. It preserves categories, rules, older names, translations, and exceptions. Import first shows a draft preview; you must save separately to keep it.
admin.policy.help.label: Write the main instruction staff will see, such as Clean up the litter. Keep it short, specific, and consistent with the chosen action type.
admin.policy.help.level0: Describe a situation with no concern present. Level 0 does not create an action. A clear definition helps avoid flagging harmless situations.
admin.policy.help.level1: Describe what severity 1 looks like for this category, using concrete, observable examples. The app uses this description to choose a level, and the rules use that level to choose an action. Make it distinct from the neighboring levels.
admin.policy.help.level2: Describe what severity 2 looks like for this category, using concrete, observable examples. The app uses this description to choose a level, and the rules use that level to choose an action. Make it distinct from the neighboring levels.
admin.policy.help.level3: Describe what severity 3 looks like for this category, using concrete, observable examples. The app uses this description to choose a level, and the rules use that level to choose an action. Make it distinct from the neighboring levels.
admin.policy.help.level4: Describe what severity 4 looks like for this category, using concrete, observable examples. The app uses this description to choose a level, and the rules use that level to choose an action. Make it distinct from the neighboring levels.
admin.policy.help.level5: Describe what severity 5 looks like for this category, using concrete, observable examples. The app uses this description to choose a level, and the rules use that level to choose an action. Make it distinct from the neighboring levels.
admin.policy.help.name: Choose a short, familiar name for this kind of issue, such as Litter. Staff see this name. If you rename a category, its old name is kept so earlier observations can still be understood.
admin.policy.help.order: A smaller number is considered first when more than one rule could apply. Usually rules should cover different situations. Change priority only for a deliberate exception, and list the affected rule references below.
admin.policy.help.overrides: List, one per line, the references of rules this exception is intentionally allowed to take priority over. The exception must have a smaller priority number. Validation still blocks any rule that can never be selected.
admin.policy.help.phone: Enter the official number the call button should open: 911, 311, or a number in 415-555-0100 format. Verify the destination before saving. The app does not place a call automatically.
admin.policy.help.prompt: Write the exact question staff will see, with a clear Yes or No answer. Every rule using this question shares this wording. If you need a different question, create a new one instead of changing a shared question’s meaning.
admin.policy.help.question: Choose a question staff must answer before this action can be selected, or choose No question required. Use a question for facts an observation may not establish, such as whether an item belongs to the site.
admin.policy.help.reason: Briefly explain why this policy is changing and what decision was made. This explanation is recorded with the prepared release so someone reviewing it later can understand the change.
admin.policy.help.reportedAt: Enter when the example observation occurred, including its time-zone offset. This checks opening-hour and weekday rules using San Francisco time. Testing does not change the saved policy.
admin.policy.help.routing: This tells the City’s 311 system which service should receive a report. Prefer an existing setting. The bulky-item and graffiti analysis options choose a more specific service from the observation. Ask the integration owner before entering a new technical code.
admin.policy.help.routingPreset: Choose an existing City reporting destination to avoid retyping its technical settings. The setting is copied into 311 routing below, where it can be reviewed.
admin.policy.help.rulesFile: Choose the rules CSV matching your categories CSV. The app checks its structure and reports problems before you save. CSV does not preserve all editor information; use JSON for a complete backup.
admin.policy.help.scenarioAnswer: Choose the answer staff would give in this example, or leave it unanswered to see which question the app asks next. This is a test answer, not a change to the question or rule.
admin.policy.help.search: Find a category by its name. This only filters the table; it does not change any categories.
admin.policy.help.severity: Choose the seriousness of the example you want to test. Levels 1–5 can produce actions; level 0 means no concern. Testing only previews the result and does not create a task or contact an agency.
admin.policy.help.severityMax: The highest severity level at which this rule applies, including that level. Together with the lowest severity, this defines the range. Other rules must cover any levels left outside this range.
admin.policy.help.severityMin: The lowest severity level at which this rule applies. Levels range from 1 to 5, with higher levels representing more serious situations. The rule also applies to every level up to the highest severity you choose.
admin.policy.help.start: The first minute when this rule applies, in San Francisco time. A start later than the end means the time period crosses midnight. Check that another rule covers times outside this period.
admin.policy.help.translation: Provide this field’s wording in the named language, keeping the same meaning and safety advice as the source. Staff using that language will see it. Source wording changes clear old translations so they can be reviewed again.
admin.policy.help.visualCues: Describe details that can actually be seen in a photo, such as scattered wrappers or a vehicle covering a curb ramp. Avoid assumptions about a person’s intentions or anything a photo cannot show.
admin.policy.help.weighting: Choose how much this category contributes to the overall condition rating. High gives it more influence than Moderate or Low. This does not determine which action staff are asked to take; the rules do that.
admin.policy.historyTruncated: Only the first 100 release records are shown.
admin.policy.importHelp: Choose a draft JSON file, or both category and rule CSVs. Import replaces your local draft preview; save explicitly to persist it. JSON preserves IDs, translations, aliases, and exceptions. CSV is a compatibility format and does not preserve all editor metadata.

rulebook.guidance.call-sfpd-non-emergenc: Call SFPD non-emergency on 415-553-0123 when sidewalk is partially or fully blocked.
rulebook.guidance.encampment-resolution-: Encampment resolution is the City's responsibility. Use the app to file a 311 ticket.
rulebook.guidance.if-an-animal-is-attack: If an animal is attacking someone, call 911 now.
rulebook.guidance.if-it-looks-unsafe-but: If it looks unsafe but nothing is on fire, and it's on the weekend, use the app to file a 311 ticket.
If it looks unsafe but nothing is on fire, and it's after business hours, use the app to file a 311 ticket.
If it looks unsafe but nothing is on fire, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm, call SFFD on 415-558-3300.
If it looks unsafe but nothing is on fire, use the app to file a 311 ticket.
rulebook.guidance.if-it-s-a-stray-or-unk: If it's a stray or unknown animal, call Animal Care and Control on 415-554-9400
rulebook.guidance.if-it-s-an-object-not-: If it's an object (not a person) blocking the path, use the app to file a 311 ticket.
rulebook.guidance.if-it-s-not-your-clien: If it's not your client, or it doesn't feel safe, call 911.
If it's not your client, report it to the City. Don't step in.
rulebook.guidance.if-it-s-your-client-an: If it's your client and it's safe, talk to them calmly. Offer to connect them with help.
rulebook.guidance.if-it-s-your-client-it: If it's your client, it's not an emergency, and it's safe, talk to them gently and offer to connect them with help.
rulebook.guidance.if-it-s-your-client-or: If it's your client or guest, and it's safe, just ask them to move.
rulebook.guidance.if-it-turns-violent-or: If it turns violent or a weapon is involved, do not get involved. Move to safety and call 911.
rulebook.guidance.if-someone-is-hurt-in-: If someone is hurt, in pain, or not waking up, call 911 now. Don't wait, even if other people are already helping.
rulebook.guidance.if-someone-is-in-real-: If someone is in real danger right now, call 911. The City will send the right team to help.
rulebook.guidance.if-someone-just-looks-: If someone just looks tired or a little unwell, check in and offer help. Keep an eye on them in case it gets worse.
rulebook.guidance.if-someone-looks-like-: If someone looks like they may be overdosing or in serious trouble, call 911 now.
rulebook.guidance.if-the-animal-belongs-: If the animal belongs to one of your clients, remind them to leash it and pick up its waste.
rulebook.guidance.if-the-graffiti-is-not: If the graffiti is not on your property, report it to the City instead of cleaning it yourself.
rulebook.guidance.if-the-graffiti-is-on-: If the graffiti is on your own building, remove it yourself within 3 days.
rulebook.guidance.if-the-item-is-yours-l: If the item is yours (like old furniture from your program), call Recology (or a private hauler) to set up a pickup.
rulebook.guidance.if-the-item-isn-t-your: If the item isn't yours, report it to the City. You don't have to move it.
rulebook.guidance.if-the-path-is-badly-b: If the path is badly blocked, or they won't move, call the SFPD non-emergency line: 415-553-0123.
rulebook.guidance.if-there-is-a-small-am: If there is a small amount of trash, pick it up yourself during your regular checks.
rulebook.guidance.if-there-is-too-much-t: If there is too much trash for you to clean up, you can use the app to file a 311 ticket and ask the City for help.
rulebook.guidance.if-they-tell-you-they-: If they tell you they need medical help, call 911 immediately.
rulebook.guidance.if-you-see-fire-smoke-: If you see fire, smoke, or something about to catch fire, call 911 now.
rulebook.guidance.illegal-parking-issues: Illegal parking issues are reported via 311, but we can't file this automatically for you. Call 311 to explain the problem.
rulebook.guidance.it-s-outside-of-animal: It's outside of Animal Care and Control opening hours. File a ticket with the City and 311 will route it appropriately.
rulebook.guidance.never-pick-up-a-needle: Never pick up a needle yourself. SFAF will come pick it up safely. Call 415-818-7769.
Never pick up a needle yourself. Use the app to file a 311 ticket so the City can safely remove it.
rulebook.guidance.potential-hate-speech-: Potential hate speech, especially on the side of a place of worship, must be investigated by the SFPD. Call 911.
rulebook.guidance.stay-away-from-it-use-: Stay away from it. Use the app to file a 311 ticket so the City can clean it up.
rulebook.guidance.when-someone-is-active: When someone is actively spraying graffiti, call the SFPD non-emergency line.
rulebook.guidance.when-the-waste-is-from: When the waste is from an animal owned by a client or resident, ask them to clean it up.
rulebook.label.ask-the-animal-s-owner-to: Ask the animal's owner to clean this up.
rulebook.label.ask-the-city-to-clean-the: Ask the City to clean the graffiti.
Ask the City to clean the street.

rulebook.label.do-not-touch-it-report-it: Do not touch it. Report it to the City.
rulebook.label.do-not-touch-the-needle-c: Do not touch the needle. Call it in to SFAF.
rulebook.label.do-not-touch-the-needle-r: Do not touch the needle. Report it to the City.
rulebook.label.don-t-remove-report-to-th: Don't remove. Report to the City.
rulebook.label.report-it-do-not-move-it-: Report it. Do not move it yourself.
rulebook.label.report-it-do-not-try-to-h: Report it. Do not try to handle it yourself.
